card.band: 8 h. Basic schemas pass fast. Union vectors, nested flatbuffer attributes, include resolution and bfbs field ordering and offsets make the full scope hard. A weaker model stops at plain tables.

Check 2: JSON-to-binary conversion on sample data is byte-equal. Check 3: invalid schemas must be rejected with the right error class. Over 1,000 cases.

The agent rebuilds `.fbs` parsing (tables, structs, unions, enums, attributes, includes, namespaces, root_type, file_identifier) and the bfbs output. facts.claim: google/flatbuffers tag v25.12.19 exists and is the upstream release
Licence is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE at top level)
src/idl_parser.cpp is about 4,574 lines (4,274 loc); the seed's 'roughly 4,000 lines' for the parser is in range, but reflection code is extra
reflection/reflection.fbs (156 lines) defines Schema, Object, Enum, Field, Service, RPCCall, Type, KeyValue, EnumVal, SchemaFile and the BaseType and AdvancedFeatures enums

The seed's count of 1,240 test files / 7,970 KB under tests

Debian packages flatbuffers-compiler (flatc) exist in the archive (forky 23.5.26, trixie 2.0.8, older rebuilds), so a flatc binary can come from distro packages; image must not contain it or its apt cache
A flatc wheel on PyPI or an npm package bundling the flatc binary
An independent from-scratch BFBS/IDL parser reimplementation exists publicly (reference for lookup)

full_card.band: Basic tables pass fast; unions, nested attributes, include resolution and bfbs field ordering/offsets are hard. Whole scope estimated 12-18 h for an excellent frontier agent: needs 20 h tier, not 8 h, or cut to core tables/enums/unions/bfbs.
full_card.build_cost: Roughly 3-5 days: snapshot surgery, stripping leaks, grader harness with 1,000 cases and byte-level oracle from pinned flatc. Smoke build not recorded ({}), so compile time is unverified.

full_card.grading_surface: Over 1,000 hidden cases: bfbs byte-equal to reference flatc; JSON-to-binary byte-equal on sample data; invalid schemas rejected with right error class.

spike_plan.kill_if: bfbs output differs across repeated runs, or the checked-in arrays_test.bfbs does not match flatc output for arrays_test.fbs (no stable byte oracle).
spike_plan.pass_if: Build finishes offline-capable with the test driver, arrays_test bfbs byte-matches flatc output, and three repeated runs are byte-identical.
steps: In a networked throwaway Linux container, clone google/flatbuffers at v25.12.19 and build flatc with CMake on 8 cores; record wall-clock time and any build errors.
Run flatc --binary --schema on tests/arrays_test.fbs and byte-compare the output to the checked-in tests/arrays_test.bfbs.
Repeat the same flatc run three times and confirm identical bfbs bytes (determinism check).
Write two small samples: one with an include and one with a union plus an attribute, and run flatc on each to confirm bfbs output is stable across runs.
Run flatc on a JSON sample for one schema and confirm binary output is stable across runs (Check 2 determinism).
Check the Debian flatbuffers-compiler package version in the target image to confirm no flatc binary or apt cache would be left in the snapshot.

v1.summary: The seed is real and sealable: upstream flatbuffers v25.12.19 is Apache-2.0 and the reference parser (idl_parser.cpp, 4,574 lines) is public, so the snapshot must strip the checked-in tests/arrays_test.bfbs and any distro flatc. The 8 h tier looks too short for the whole parser-plus-bfbs scope (estimated about 14 frontier hours), so I recommend the 20 h tier or a cut to core tables, enums, unions and bfbs; the spike should confirm byte-stable oracle output first.

v2.note: Real C++ parser rebuild with a confirmed 4,574-line reference and a generator-driven surface. The 20 h tier matches the 14 h frontier estimate. Review risk: byte-identical bfbs and JSON binaries depend on the order of builder calls, so a valid parser that serializes differently would fail. Compare decoded reflection objects and decoded buffers instead, and keep byte-equality as an optional bucket. Strip tests/arrays_test.bfbs, the generated bfbs files and any Debian flatc. idl_gen_* depends on the Parser API in idl.h, so ship that header as the contract.
